chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he prayed the final 'Isha prayer, would retire to his bed and would not pray anything until after the middle of the night, whether in the month of Ramadan or in other months.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about praying night prayer in the summer during the short nights, specifically praying night prayer at the beginning of the night. He said: 'Yes, good is what you saw and good is what you did.'
And that which clarifies what we mentioned is that this ruling is specific to the state of travel and necessity.
ai.seo_question: When did the Prophet Muhammad typically pray his night prayer, and how does this change in summer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) flexible approach to *Tahajjud*, distinguishing between his general practice of praying after midnight and the concession to pray earlier during short summer nights or travel. Shia scholars utilize this text to demonstrate that while delaying night prayer is preferred, praying at the beginning of the night is equally valid and praiseworthy, particularly when circumstances like heat or travel make it difficult. The hadith underscores the practicality of Islamic jurisprudence, balancing spiritual devotion with physical ease.
